summary: 交换名片的礼仪因国而异，却一直是商业交往的常见开场。作者认为实体卡片既能留下不同的视觉记忆，又能自然地开启交谈，全球化和智能手机的普及没有消除这些社交需求。
logic: 回顾名片历史及创意设计
电子交换引出纸卡存废之争
从记忆、破冰和关系建立解释其延续

paragraphs.brief: 这种仪式可能是普遍的，但是，贺卡的细节和交换方式因国家而异。
sentences: The ritual may be universal, but the details of business cards and how they are swapped vary across countries.
这种仪式可能是普遍的，但是，贺卡的细节和交换方式因国家而异。
Americans throw their cards casually across a table; the Japanese make the exchange of cards a formal ceremony.
美国人随意把牌扔到桌子上；日本人把换牌变成正式仪式。
While there are cards that are discreet and understated, others are crammed full of details and titles.
虽然有些卡片是谨慎的和低调的，但另一些卡片则充斥着细节和标题。

Some businesspeople hand out 24-carat gold cards, and there are kindergarten children who have cards with not only their own contact details, but also with the job descriptions of their parents and even grandparents.
有些商人发放了24克拉的金卡，有些幼儿园儿童不仅有自己的详细联系方式，而且还有父母甚至祖父母的工作说明。
This practice has become so common in parts of New York, for example, that the use of such cards is now prohibited by some of these institutions.
例如，在纽约一些地方，这种做法已司空见惯，一些这类机构现在禁止使用这种卡片。

paragraphs.brief: 然后，在17世纪，欧洲商人发明了一种新型卡片，作为微型广告，标志着商业卡片的到来。
sentences: Cards have been around a long time in one form or another.
贺卡以这种或那种形式存在了很长一段时间。
The Chinese invented calling cards in the 15th century to give people notice that they intended to pay them a visit, but these were for social purposes only.
中国人发明了15世纪的电话卡，让人们知道他们打算去拜访他们，但是这些只是为了社会目的。
Then, in the 17th century, European businesspeople invented a new type of card to act as miniature advertisements, signalling the advent of the business card.
然后，在17世纪，欧洲商人发明了一种新型卡片，作为微型广告，标志着商业卡片的到来。
In today’s world, business cards can cause people to have strong emotional reactions.
在当今世界，名片可以使人们产生强烈的情绪反应。
According to one experienced company director, very few things can provoke more heated discussion at a board meeting than the composition of the company’s business cards.
据一位经验丰富的公司经理说，在董事会会议上，很少有事情比公司名片的构成更能引起热烈的讨论。

paragraphs.brief: 许多公司试图通过改变卡片的形式来提升自己。
sentences: Lots of companies try to promote themselves by altering the form of the card.
许多公司试图通过改变卡片的形式来提升自己。
Employees at one famous toy company give out little plastic figures with their contact details stamped on them.
一家著名的玩具公司的雇员们提供一些塑料图上面贴有他们的联系方式
One fast-food company has business cards which are shaped like a portion of French fries.
一家快餐公司有名片形状像炸薯条
A Canadian divorce lawyer once gave out cards that could be torn in two – one half for each of the spouses.
一名加拿大离婚律师曾经给过一张卡片，每张卡片可能被撕成两半，每张半。
For many business commentators, such gimmicky business cards prove that the use of a physical business card is nearly at an end.
对许多商业评论家来说，这种闪烁的名片证明实际名片的使用已接近尾声。
After all, why bother exchanging bits of thick paper at all when you can simply swap electronic versions by smartphone?
毕竟，当你可以简单的用智能手机交换电子版本时，为什么要费心交换厚厚的纸？

paragraphs.brief: 但是，人们也可以提出相反的论点：名片是在这里停留的，在一个充满会议和信函的商业世界中，你的名片是独一无二的，这一点比以往任何时候都更加重要。
sentences: However, one can just as well argue the opposite: that business cards are here to stay, and, in a business world full of meetings and correspondence, it is more important than ever that your card is unique.
但是，人们也可以提出相反的论点：名片是在这里停留的，在一个充满会议和信函的商业世界中，你的名片是独一无二的，这一点比以往任何时候都更加重要。
Attempts to reinvent business cards for the digital age have not been successful.
为数字时代重塑名片的努力没有成功。
Even at the latest technology conferences, people still greet each other by handing out little rectangles made from paper rather than using a digital alternative.
即使在最新的技术会议上，人们仍然通过散发纸上的小矩形来互相打招呼，而不是使用数字替代。

paragraphs.brief: 要了解名片，就必须了解企业如何运作。
sentences: To understand business cards, it is necessary to understand how business works.
要了解名片，就必须了解企业如何运作。
That business cards are thriving in a digital age is a forceful reminder that there is much about business that is timeless.
数字时代的名片蓬勃发展有力地提醒人们，很多商业是永恒的。
According to Kate Jones, a business lecturer, there is one eternal and inescapable issue.
据商业讲师Kate Jones说，有一个永恒和不可回避的问题。
Her 2006 study of more than 200 business executives in North America found that trust was the key element for running a successful business.
她2006年对北美200多名企业主管的研究发现，信任是经营成功企业的关键因素。
It is vital to be able to look someone in the eye and decide what sort of person they are.
关键是能够直视某人的眼睛并且决定他们是什么人
In this way, you can transform acquaintanceships into relationships.
这样，你就可以把熟人变成关系了

A good proportion of business life will always be about building social connections – having dinner or playing sport with clients and colleagues – and while computers can deal with administrative tasks, it is still human beings that have to focus on the emotional.
商业生活的一大部分将永远是建立社会联系 — — 与客户和同事一起吃晚饭或玩游戏 — —。虽然计算机可以处理行政任务，但人类仍然必须关注情绪问题。

paragraphs.brief: 查看不同的卡片可以提高你的记忆力仅仅通过统一的电子名单就不会这样了
sentences: The rapid advance of globalisation means that this relationship-building process is becoming ever more demanding.
全球化的迅速推进意味着建立关系的进程正变得越来越艰巨。
Managers have to put more effort in when dealing with international counterparts, especially when there is not a common language, which is so often the case these days.
管理人员在与国际对应方打交道时必须作出更大努力，特别是在没有共同语言的情况下，这在当今经常发生。
A recent UK survey showed that chief executives of global organisations now routinely spend three out of every four weeks on international travel.
联合王国最近的一项调查显示，全球组织的行政首长现在通常每四个星期花三星期时间进行国际旅行。
It is in these situations that business cards are doubly useful, as they are a quick way of establishing connections.
正是在这些情况下，名片具有双重用途，因为它们是建立联系的快速途径。
Cards can also remind you that you have actually met someone in a face-to-face meeting rather than just searched for them on the Internet.
贺卡还可以提醒你，你实际上在面对面的会面中遇到了一个人，而不只是在互联网上搜索。
Looking through piles of different cards can enhance your memory in ways that simply looking through uniform electronic lists would never do.
查看不同的卡片可以提高你的记忆力仅仅通过统一的电子名单就不会这样了

paragraphs.brief: 珍妮特·麦金泰尔是当今世界名片领域的领先专家。
sentences: Janet McIntyre is a leading expert on business cards in today’s world.
珍妮特·麦金泰尔是当今世界名片领域的领先专家。
She maintains that as companies become more complex, cards are essential in determining the exact status of every contact you meet in multinational corporations.
她认为，随着公司变得更加复杂，卡片对于确定你们在多国公司中遇到的每一个联系人的确切地位至关重要。
Janet also explains how exchanging business cards can be an effective way of initiating a conversation, because it gives people a ritual to follow when they first meet a new business contact.
珍妮特也解释了交换名片如何成为启动对话的有效方式，因为它让人们有一个仪式跟随他们第一次遇到新的商业联系人。

paragraphs.brief: 商业界对创造和发明新事物的想法非常着迷，这些新事物将改变我们的一切工作方式，这确实导致进步。
sentences: The business world is obsessed with the idea of creating and inventing new things that will change the way we do everything, and this does lead to progress.
商业界对创造和发明新事物的想法非常着迷，这些新事物将改变我们的一切工作方式，这确实导致进步。
But there are lots of things that do not need to be changed and, in Janet McIntyre’s view, tradition also has an equally valuable role to play.
但是，有许多事情不需要改变，在珍妮特·麦金泰尔看来，传统也具有同等宝贵的作用。
Therefore the practice of exchanging business cards is likely to continue in the business world.
因此，商业界可能继续采用交换名片的做法。

items.zh: 有些幼儿园禁止儿童取得名片。
items.why: 纽约部分幼儿园禁止孩子使用这种卡片，直接印证“有些幼儿园禁止”。

items.en: It was the Chinese who first began the practice of using business cards.
items.zh: 是中国人先开始使用名片的
items.why: 古代中国使用的是社交拜访卡；把卡片当作小广告的商务名片则由欧洲商人发明。

items.en: Designing business cards can be a controversial process for some companies.
items.zh: 对一些公司来说，设计名片可能是一个有争议的过程。

items.en: A famous toy company has boosted its sales by using one type of unusual business card.
items.zh: 一家著名的玩具公司通过使用一种不寻常的名片提高了销售量。
items.why: 玩具公司发放印有联系方式的塑料小人，文章没有提供这种名片提高销量的证据。

items.en: Some business commentators predict a decline in the use of paper business cards.
items.zh: 一些商业评论家预测纸质名片的使用会减少。
items.why: 一些商业评论者认为实体名片的使用已接近尾声，与预期纸质名片使用下降一致。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

points: 古代中国使用的是社交拜访卡；把卡片当作小广告的商务名片则由欧洲商人发明。
回到对应内容“她2006年对北美200多名企业主管的研究发现，信任是经营成功企业的关键因素”，再按题干要求写出答案。
clauses: …, others are crammed full of details and titles.
连接词 while 引出“While there are cards that are discreet and understated”，说明主句的时间或对比关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 while 把这一层关系补进去。
This practice has become so common in parts of New York, for example, ….
“that the use of such cards is now prohibited by some of these institutions”补足 become 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 become 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
lead: The exchange of business cards is as close to a universal ritual as you can find in the business world.
交换名片是接近于一个普遍仪式的，商业界可以找到。
